connectedHome.composition: ConnectedHomeWorkspace composes the existing HomeScreen, Constellation, PlaceDetail, Bloom, attention and Customize controls with the existing semantic light/dark resources and Outfit/DM Sans roles.
connectedHome.destinations: Connected mode hides synthetic Story and Control lab. A written task-activity-not-connected notice replaces the sample LuciaNow stages. Explore the demo remains explicit.
connectedHome.reportLifetime: Credential-bound reads refresh every 20 seconds in the foreground. Five-second ticks reproject report age including read duration. Current can become Stale. No revision stream is implemented.
connectedHome.qualification: Current, Stale, Unknown and Unavailable describe source reports. Connected observations use Reported time. Capture time and Reported time do not establish physical verification, safety or presence.
connectedHome.recovery: Read failure and suspend clear reports, source choices and selection. Resume rechecks access. Retry Home reports and Connection are explicit recovery actions. Revoked or changed authority returns to Connection. No synthetic fallback or offline grant exists.
connectedHome.persistence: Local metadata is scoped by canonical host, home, member and exact Home place/field grants. Catalogs and reports are not saved. SourcePlaceId preserves exact authorized source-place provenance; moved or missing sources require explicit binding review.

homeImport.layout: 16-unit margin, 1040-unit maximum content width, vertical scrolling and wrapping footer actions. Selection and review share equal columns with a 24-unit gap only at width >= 900 and mapped body text <= 20; phone and large-text layouts use separate steps.
homeImport.rows: Existing household outline icons, semantic resources and native form controls. Selection, TextBox, icon chooser, source Expander and theme-button targets have a 48-unit minimum height. Sources to bind expands the exact source names and roles.
homeImport.review: Preview counts new places, new bindings and assignments kept elsewhere. Existing names, icons, order, connections, missing bindings and source ownership remain. Conflicts name the current owner and say No reassignment. Selection edits invalidate preview.
homeImport.application: Add to draft applies only to the unchanged reviewed setup draft and writes no file. Save setup remains the persistence step with existing discard protection and revision-conflict recovery. Import neither grants access nor infers readings or physical neighbors.
homeImport.focus: Preview focuses the review title. Compact Change selection or Back returns to selection and focuses a selected place. Leaving import restores the setup import action. Invalid selection focuses written ProblemBrush status.

connectedHomeEvidence.disposition: ship, independent finish review, no material fixes

nativeTests.scope: Includes opt-in actual UI, Windows DPAPI, HTTPS, SQLite and HA-wire synthetic-fixture checks.

connectedHomeEvidence.evidenceLocation: Captures and review evidence are retained outside the public repository.
connectedHomeEvidence.limits: Successful connected Home visual coverage is narrower than the import/recovery matrix. No actual-household, installed Android TLS, iOS, hardware, TalkBack, safe-area or performance qualification follows. Story, Week and Engine remain unfinished.

components.name: ConnectionScreen
components.description: Static illustrative connection specimen using the built panel, Outfit/DM Sans roles, authored Home path and semantic palette. Native UI starts with protected restore and provides form, approval, verified, recovery and removal states. Canonical host and submitted device identity remain with the code, exact grants expand under Approved access, and written status distinguishes local forgetting from host revocation. This preview performs no authentication and stores no credentials. Native expanded layout starts at control width 960 only when mapped status body text is at most 20 units; larger text stacks. CSS media width is only a normal-size approximation. Native stage focus, platform text mapping, protected storage and protocol belong to Avalonia and Connection, not this specimen. Owners now use Companion devices on the trusted HTTPS dashboard for code review, exact grants and issued-session management. The native footer directs them there without a style change. The owner UI has a scoped ship disposition. Open Home now opens the credential-bound ConnectedHomeWorkspace and verifies authorized reports before showing the shared Home. Story, Week, Engine and platform/release qualification remain unfinished. Earlier connection/recovery preview and owner UI ship dispositions remain scoped; the connected Home/import extension has its own ship disposition. This static pairing specimen still displays no household reports.

components.name: CompanionShell and HomeSaveConflictScreen
components.description: Illustrative representation of the implemented Options, Setup and Story/Home shell. Native Options has an Appearance submenu for System, Light and Dark, plus Customize Home and Connection. Only explicit demo mode exposes Story and Control lab; connected mode exposes Refresh Home reports. Options > Connection returns to the cached ConnectionScreen; the app now starts there and demo entry is explicit. Setup disables Setup, Story, Customize Home and Control lab until Save/Cancel. Browser disclosure, focus and font fallback approximate native controls. The snippet does not navigate, change the native theme or save. Native Back/Escape closes Home actions, compact detail and then expanded Customize, returns Story or Control lab to Home, and remains unhandled at Home root with no open context for the OS. Dirty setup has a discard question. One Android activity view is cached only in-process; no unsaved draft is stored on disk. AndroidManifest temporarily sets android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback=false because default predictive Back bypassed callbacks in the API 36 emulator. The checked APK returns native Garden detail to Home with this compatibility opt-out. Predictive Back gesture animation remains unqualified. A density change/reset recorded same-process activity destruction/recreation with draft retention; this is not disk persistence. Customize Home returns to Home, closes detail/actions, expands the footer and brings it into view with focus. A final debug APK on a dedicated API 36 emulator opened and scrolled Customize Home through Options, moved Lucia now earlier to produce Places, LuciaNow, Attention, and retained the chosen order through Save and force-stop/cold restart. This supplements desktop/headless evidence; it does not qualify physical devices, TalkBack, iOS, performance or whole-application completion. The default shell now passes SampleObservationSources to the local binding editor. These Sample-named choices remain synthetic discovery inputs. Connected setup now uses its verified authorized catalog and reviewed HomeImportScreen, with no sample substitution. HomeSaveConflictScreen is implemented local revision-conflict recovery. A stale byte revision pauses autosave and exposes Review save conflict; regular storage I/O failures retain Retry save. The review hides the duplicate footer, disables Setup/Story/Customize/Control lab, preserves Appearance, and focuses its title after reading. It compares session and saved metadata with accessible Places and bindings Expanders and named wrapping buttons. Back/Back without choosing preserves both alternatives; Read saved setup again refreshes without choosing. Replace writes the complete session against the reviewed revision, while Discard/load requires a readable same-home profile. Stale choices refresh without applying either decision. Missing files can be recreated explicitly; corrupt safely snapshotted bytes can be replaced explicitly; different-home profiles have written cannot-load guidance with loading disabled. Oversized/access-failed unsnapshotted files disable both choices. No automatic merge or durable unsaved draft is implemented. The HTML below illustrates the different-home review state with disabled loading; it does not perform file I/O, revision checks or navigation. This C04 record uses source and desktop/headless captures, not an installed-APK or physical-device claim.

components.name: Home graph and HomeSectionOrder
components.description: Illustrative static representation of stable varied place positions, authored icon paths and configured neighbor lines. Native ConstellationPanel measures child sizes and expands its normal 108-unit slots and 152-unit child-width cap by the largest orb FontSize / 16 ratio. It preserves supplied order, allows at most three columns below its own 800-unit width and four above, and wraps larger homes. The native Home badge stacks below the name at Home width below 600 when the mapped name font exceeds 32. Lines and the faint dot field are decorative; this SVG is not the native layout engine or a floor plan. HomeSectionOrder is the actual scrolling Customize footer Expander, also reached through Options. It changes a validated permutation of Your places, Needs a look and Lucia now using named 48-unit-minimum earlier/later Buttons with authored 20-unit outline paths. Boundaries disable, Restore default order disables at the default, and moving retains available focus and brings it into view. Phone follows all three preferred sections; expanded Home promotes the first while retaining Places in the wide column, with the remaining section and detail at the side. Order saves in an optional version-1 local metadata field, missing values default, and loading a saved order does not initiate a save. Restore default order is a preference change and uses the normal save path. The additional HTML details element illustrates the native Expander; movement is static in this preview and does not persist preferences. The Restore default order caption is a wrapping native TextBlock with an explicit button accessible name; clipping is not a design rule. Connected Home reuses this composition with a Connected badge and report-capture notice. Its badge obeys the same stacking rule; it shows no synthetic task stages. ConnectedHomeWorkspace retains the existing scrolling Home reports recovery view. Each active subscriber conditionally reads every 20 seconds using a weak session/home/member/exact-grant/content ETag that excludes capture time. Changed or unknown revisions return a full replacement; 304 confirms only the in-memory snapshot and preserves capture time and the monotonic age baseline. Five-second age ticks include the original read duration, so unchanged reports can become Stale. There is no delta replay, push stream or atomic upstream snapshot promise. Failure or suspend clears the snapshot, revision, reports, catalog and selection. Recovery and resume recheck protected identity and access before an unconditional read. Transport failures and HTTP 408, 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504 retry at 20, 40, 80, 160 and 300 seconds, capped at 300 unless Retry-After requests longer. Monotonic server waits survive manual retry and suspend/resume. Denial, protected-storage, invalid-response and bounded-capacity failures do not auto-loop. Retry Home reports disables while busy or under a server wait; Connection stays enabled. Recovery status receives focus once on entry, not on timer updates. The same setup editor and unsaved input return after recovery, in process memory only. The 24 reviewed native desktop/headless captures cover recovery and restored setup at widths 390 and 1000, both themes and normal/doubled text. Finish review returned ship with no material visual fixes. At width 390 with doubled text, source-failure actions continue below the first viewport in the vertical scroll region. Physical scrolling, restored-editor keyboard focus, successful-Home visual coverage and installed-APK TLS remain unqualified by this matrix. This static graph specimen does not implement conditional requests, recovery, native focus or platform behavior.

components.name: Home setup and SourceBindingPicker
components.description: Illustrative representation of native labelled TextBoxes, place list or compact chooser, icon ComboBox and neighbor CheckBoxes. Source changes at the editor's 800-unit Bounds.Width, keeps Save and Cancel outside the scrolling form, and uses named draft actions and inline warnings. Browser field appearance is approximate. No save, import, bindings or persistence is implemented by the snippet. Native setup scrolls the header with the forms. Back/Escape checks raw uncommitted fields as well as applied draft changes, first hides removal confirmation, and then asks Keep editing or Discard changes when dirty. The question disables editing, hides normal Save/Cancel commands and focuses Keep editing. Explicit Cancel still exits immediately. The separate static question below illustrates this state; the preview does not implement Back or draft persistence. SourceBindingPicker is implemented below physical-neighbor controls in the scrolling place form. Source and Reports are named 48-unit-minimum native ComboBoxes. Supported roles come only from the selected source; a new source clears the role choice, Reports disables without a source and Bind source disables without a role. Existing role/source rows have explicit named Remove binding buttons. Missing catalog sources or unsupported stored roles remain visible with muted written warnings, not inferred readings. Binding changes are draft metadata until Save, protected by Back, and deleting a place prunes its bindings. A source-role pair is unique across the home; conflicts require explicit removal at the current owner. The demo shell supplies Sample-named synthetic catalog choices. Connected setup supplies the verified authorized catalog and opens HomeImportScreen for reviewed additions. Only binding IDs/roles and optional SourcePlaceId provenance persist, not the catalog or values. The static preview neither edits topology nor grants access. A final debug APK on a dedicated API 36 emulator showed the sample source catalog, offered only Temperature for Sample temperature sensor, added its binding and retained the living-room binding plus chosen Home section order through Save and a force-stop/cold restart. Scoped JSON inspection confirmed metadata only, without observations or catalog values. These bounded installed-APK results supplement native desktop/headless captures; physical-device, TalkBack, iOS, performance and full-application qualification remain open. Rejected cross-place source-role assignments leave metadata unchanged and show an inline wrapping, focusable BindingError in ProblemBrush. The native picker focuses and scrolls this local owner/removal guidance into view rather than the editor header; visible error prevents Source focus from overriding it. Choosing source/role clears the error. Successful operations retain their normal Source-focus behavior. The static error preview keeps a supported Contact role and Sample gate contact source selected, with Bind source enabled, to represent the rejected assignment state.

Native StoryOrbit draws at most six visible place rings, hour ticks, recorded arcs and quality dashes on elapsed-home-day coordinates. The exact native ring geometry, shared selection and optional 280ms CubicEaseOut hand transition belong to Avalonia. A native slider and named chapter/report buttons supply time input; the preview slider does not update the drawing. Sample date, timezone and explicit no-live-data statement are retained. Expanded native layout uses a 400-unit dial at Story width 900; compact dial is clamped to 240..340. All-place timelines remain available beyond six rings. At mapped CenterTime.FontSize > 36, the native selected time and offset move below the dial and its center caption reads Time below. The normal-size SVG preview does not implement platform scaling or this conditional layout.

narrative.overview:
Places use household outline icons, written names and explicit state labels. Their circles distinguish activity, unavailability and selection. The Observatory palette gives them quiet, warm surroundings in dark mode and pale, neutral surroundings in light mode. Outfit names screens and sections. DM Sans carries readings, control labels and explanations.

The app opens on ConnectionScreen and checks protected storage before showing a host form or verified connection. Owners review codes, choose exact grants and manage issued sessions in Companion devices on the trusted HTTPS dashboard. Open Home reads authorized source reports into the existing Constellation Home, with qualified readings, local setup, source bindings, save-conflict recovery and Customize section ordering. Bring your places in lets the user select authorized places, preview exact metadata additions and conflicts, add to the setup draft, then use the existing Save setup action. Import preserves existing names, icons, order, connections and source ownership. A saved binding grants no access. While active, connected Home checks report revisions and keeps their original age. Temporary read failures show automatic-retry guidance; server waits disable retry without hiding Connection.

Explore the demo explicitly opens the cached synthetic shell with its offline badge and synthetic reading time. That mode retains HomeConstellation, PlaceDetail, contextual Bloom actions, offline StoryOrbit Day and the control workbench. Story links a one-day dial, authored chapters and readable place timelines through one selection state. Connected mode shares the Home composition but hides sample Story and Control lab and replaces the sample task stages with a written activity-not-connected notice. The scoped connected Home and import extension has a ship disposition. BUILD-PLAN.md still owns the unfinished Story, Week and Engine adapters and the remaining motion, performance, platform and release gates.

Native sources own this system: `Lucia.Companion.App/App.axaml`, `CompanionTypography.cs`, `Styles/Controls.axaml`, `CompanionShell.axaml`, the files in `Screens/` and `Controls/`, and `ControlWorkbench.axaml`. Frontmatter lengths use CSS-compatible px notation for interchange. In native source these are Avalonia device-independent units, not physical screen pixels. Font sizes record the normal-size baseline; Android maps each text role through its native SP converter. The sidecar HTML/CSS snippets are illustrative normal-size representations for a design panel. They do not drive the native UI or qualify TalkBack, real-device accessibility, iOS, safe areas or performance.
keyCharacteristics: Place icons pair names and written states with distinct state and selection rings.
Semantic brushes switch together between light and dark.
Observations distinguish current readings from last-known values and unknown times.
Home and setup use separate native width thresholds for compact and expanded layouts.
Configured connections and stable offsets give the home graph structure without a floor-plan claim.
Contextual Bloom actions surround the selected place icon at normal text sizes and become a readable action list at large text sizes.
Story keeps reported intervals, last-known values and missing reports visibly distinct.
Home and Bloom remain static; Story optionally transitions only its selected time hand.
Platform text settings resize individual type roles, with layout adaptations for larger text.
Customize changes the order of the three Home sections without hiding any section or rearranging places.
Source-binding metadata remains separate from physical neighbors, source access and qualified readings.
Import separates place selection from exact addition/conflict review before applying metadata to the setup draft.
Connected Home keeps report quality, original age and reported time visible; read failures clear reports and show deliberate recovery.
Save-conflict recovery shows both metadata alternatives and requires an explicit checked choice.
Connection keeps the canonical HTTPS host and submitted device name beside the approval code.
Verified access discloses exact grants without substituting sample household data.
Recovery distinguishes retry, local forgetting and a request to revoke the device session.

rules.name: The Written State Rule
rules.body: Every place color has a visible state label. Color alone cannot distinguish Quiet from Unavailable or Changed from Waiting.

rules.name: The Two Family Rule
rules.body: Use Outfit for titles and section headings, and DM Sans for control labels, readings and supporting text.

rules.name: The Native Text Rule
rules.body: Bind text to its matching TextSize resource. Keep geometry independent of the platform's per-role text mapping, and adapt constrained compositions when text needs more room.

rules.name: The Stable Home Rule
rules.body: Preserve explicit room order through selection, pinning and state display. Place reordering belongs to setup's Move earlier and Move later controls. Customize changes section order independently of room order.

rules.name: The Independent Tracks Rule
rules.body: A report on one track supplies no evidence for another. Unmarked ring portions mean no supplied report, and dotted timeline guides remain unknown until a report covers them.

rules.name: The Still Observatory Rule
rules.body: Home, place states and Bloom remain static. Story may transition its dial hand for 280 milliseconds with native CubicEaseOut when selection changes. The "Animate the time hand" checkbox below the timelines disables that transition. Reports, chapters and time selection remain usable without motion; no automatic playback or rotating carousel exists.

dos: Do use the semantic brush pairs for light and dark rather than hardcoding a single theme into a native control.
Do show each place's name and written state alongside its icon.
Do retain the explicit DM Sans body-size override on theme buttons.
Do keep observation quality, last-known values and observation time visible.
Do identify demo Home, Story and workbench data as synthetic before their observations or history.
Do use the authored household paths for the implemented place icons.
Do preserve explicit place order and keep pinning independent of graph position.
Do keep Home's circular selection ring distinct from its rectangular keyboard-focus frame.
Do attach Bloom to the selected icon, keep its named actions legible and restore focus when dismissed.
Do keep all place timelines reachable when the dial's six-ring budget is exceeded.
Do preserve separate evidence tracks, full local time ranges, offsets, quality and source help.
Do provide the native slider and chapter/report buttons alongside decorative dial input.
Do keep the Story hand transition optional with the visible animation checkbox.
Do use dynamic TextSize resources for platform-adjusted type and let constrained layouts adapt.
Do keep all Bloom actions reachable in its large-text list.
Do preserve pending setup changes on Back until the user chooses Discard changes.
Do keep every Home section present when reordering and expose named movement controls with disabled boundaries.
Do retain missing source bindings with a written warning and require explicit removal.
Do show both local metadata alternatives and recheck the reviewed revision before a save-conflict choice.
Do keep canonical host, submitted device name, code expiry and exact approved grants readable in connection states.
Do distinguish local forgetting from confirmed host revocation and keep removal choices explicit.
Do preview exact selected-place additions and source conflicts before Add to draft, then require Save setup for persistence.
Do preserve existing place metadata and source ownership during import, and require explicit review for moved sources.
Do show connected report quality, Reported time and capture time with the existing Home controls.
Do clear reports on read failure or suspend and recheck protected identity and access before an unconditional recovery read.
Do retain original report age and capture time after an unchanged-revision response.
Do respect server-requested waits across retry and resume, and keep Connection available.
Do retain the current setup editor and unsaved input through temporary report recovery.
donts: Don't use color as the only indication of place state or selection.
Don't promote an old reading to the current-value position.
Don't infer locked from closed, occupancy from Quiet, or a physical result from a completed request.
Don't present connected Home and reviewed metadata import as completion of Story, Week, Engine or the wider native app.
Don't replace a failed household connection with an automatic synthetic Home.
Don't claim real-device accessibility, safe-area or performance qualification from desktop renders.
Don't treat illustrative sidecar HTML/CSS or generated color ramps as native implementation tokens.
Don't treat configured graph connections or static layout offsets as a measured floor plan.
Don't treat unmarked ring segments, unknown track spans or absent chapters as proof that nothing happened.
Don't convert motion report buckets into occupancy or continuous presence.
Don't claim live history, persisted history or a historical binding policy from the authored Story fixture.
Don't treat the in-process activity-view cache as persisted unsaved drafts.
Don't claim TalkBack, device, iOS or performance qualification from text-resource mapping or headless checks.
Don't confuse Home section order with the stable order of places in the graph.
Don't infer source ownership from physical adjacency or promote a saved binding into a current reading.
Don't merge save-conflict metadata automatically or replace an unread file without a safely captured revision.
Don't present memory-only session changes as durable unsaved-draft recovery.
Don't show sample Story, task stages or Control lab inside connected mode.
Don't treat saved bindings, a previous report or an old grant as permission to display an offline household.
Don't treat revisioned polling as event replay, a push stream or an atomic Home Assistant snapshot.
